summary.headline: HCC Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 993 crore with EBITDA margin down to 10.7% from 14.9%, while order intake lagged the Rs 15,000 crore FY27 target.
summary.overview: Management reported standalone turnover of Rs 982 crore and standalone net profit of Rs 37 crore, with consolidated PAT of Rs 51 crore on revenue of Rs 993 crore. EBITDA margin fell to 10.7% from 14.9% a year earlier, which management attributed to about Rs 8,000 crore of recently won projects still in mobilisation with costs running ahead of revenue. Order intake in the quarter was thin: one Bhutan order of Rs 127 crore, with L1 positions of about Rs 2,241 crore (HCC share Rs 1,672 crore) and bids of about Rs 10,000 crore under evaluation. Management reiterated the Rs 15,000 crore order inflow target and a 13-14% EBITDA margin run rate, and said Rs 100 crore of debt would be prepaid in August 2026.

financial_highlights.change: Margin described as improved; no YoY figure stated

segments.name: Order book and pipeline
segments.commentary: Order backlog spread across transport, hydro, water, nuclear and buildings; about Rs 13,000 crore per analyst question, with roughly Rs 8,000 crore won in the last 15 months still in mobilisation. Average execution period put at about 3.5 years.

segments.name: Hydro and tunnelling projects
segments.commentary: Vishnugad Pipalkoti about 85% complete with dam nearly 85% done; Bhivpuri powerhouse excavation underway; NTPC Tapovan Vishnugad breakthrough achieved in phases 2 and 3.

segments.name: Metro projects
segments.commentary: Indore Metro TBM deployment advanced; Patna Metro PC05 and PC06 mobilisation under way after client handed over workspaces; Agardanda marine and land foundation works in full swing with statutory clearances expected by November 2026.

segments.name: Industrial and nuclear
segments.commentary: Aditya Aluminium pot shell and superstructure fabrication started; nuclear activity is at pre-order stage pending SHANTI Act rules, with management expecting significant nuclear orders in FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow target of about Rs 15,000 crore reiterated, with management saying some bids had slipped by about two months.
EBITDA margin run rate of 13-14% to be maintained by year end; management says full-year average margin will be in the mid-teens, with some quarters below average.
FY27 revenue expected broadly flat versus last year, with a possible upside of 15-20% (about Rs 400-500 crore) depending on mobilisation.
Medium-term growth target of 20-25% (said to be 15-25% depending on period), with 20%+ the stated aim, but no formal FY28 guidance given.
Debt reduction: Rs 100 crore prepayment in August 2026 with larger prepayments under way; management aims to be near debt-free over time, with exact figures to be given next quarter.
Arbitration awards of about Rs 1,700 crore expected to be realised over three to four years; Rs 600 crore fund mobilisation approved by the board but not yet decided.
capex_capacity: Indore Metro: TBM deployment at an advanced stage and tunnel ring preparation under way; station excavation in full swing.
Vishnugad Pipalkoti: machine halls for units 2 and 3 in advanced construction, surge shaft advanced, dam about 85% complete, overall project about 85% complete.
Agardanda: segment production for bridge erection under way; statutory clearances expected by November 2026, with some policy clearances still awaited.
Patna Metro: segment casting yard and infrastructure being set up for PC05 and PC06; traffic diversion work in progress.
Nuclear: management says HCC has built about 55-60% of existing power plants in India; plans to team up with partners to take on larger scopes.
demand_pricing: Order intake in Q1 was limited: one Bhutan order of Rs 127 crore, and an L1 position of Rs 2,241 crore (HCC share Rs 1,672 crore) pending conversion.
Serco order of about Rs 1,100 crore won in April 2026 is already in the order book, not in L1.
Bids under evaluation total about Rs 10,000 crore (HCC share about Rs 7,750 crore); total pipeline of about Rs 86,000 crore.
Pipeline traction is strongest in hydropower, then underground metro and urban transit, with industrial and metal orders and nuclear also in view.
Target EBITDA margin for new projects is 13-14%; management says it will be selective on pricing and client quality.
Management says about 90% of focus is domestic India; no current Middle East pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Shukla attributed it to about Rs 8,000 crore of projects won in the last 15 months being in mobilisation, where costs are incurred before margin contribution; margin is expected to recover to 13-14%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 15,000 crore order target achievable given weak Q1 intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Santosh Rai said the target is maintained, citing about Rs 10,000 crore of bids under evaluation, though some large bids were delayed by about two months; new bid submissions are expected within two to three months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,700 crore arbitration receivable realisable and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Shukla said realisation over three to four years is reasonable; Arjun Dhawan noted government Vivad-se-Vishwas settlements at 65-85% of award amounts could be considered case by case.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt is left and when will it be cleared?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Shukla said total debt is about Rs 2,000 crore; a Rs 100 crore prepayment is planned in August 2026, and a precise deleveraging figure is expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is HCC's nuclear opportunity and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Santosh Rai said the government plans 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047 against 9 GW today, costing about Rs 18-22 crore per MW; HCC is positioned mainly in civil works and is teaming up for larger scopes, with industry expecting rules by end of the parliamentary session or winter session.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter stake reduction and pledges?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Shukla said promoters have subscribed to rights issues and pledges are to HCC lenders and will be removed as debt is prepaid; Arjun Dhawan said the family remains committed and will evaluate increasing its stake.

risks_watch: Order inflow: Q1 intake was thin and the Rs 15,000 crore FY27 target depends on converting about Rs 10,000 crore of bids under evaluation and new bids slipping by about two months.
Margin execution: EBITDA margin of 10.7% against a 13-14% target; the recovery depends on mobilised projects moving into revenue and any quarter-to-quarter pattern of below-average margins.
Receivables and arbitration: about Rs 1,700 crore of awards under challenge in court; timing of cash is 3-4 years and settlements may involve haircuts.
Promoter stake and pledges: management did not state the current stake or pledge level; pledges are linked to HCC lenders and expected to lift on prepayment.
Nuclear timing: orders depend on SHANTI Act rules, with private orders expected six to eight months after the rules are published.
Fund raise: Rs 600 crore board-approved mobilisation not yet decided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the longer-term pipeline and deleveraging, but defensive on the Q1 margin fall and thin order intake; several answers were non-committal on accounting treatment, debt prepayment size and FY28 growth.
key_quotes: Almost Rs. 8,000 crores in our order book are projects which we have acquired during last 15-month period.
I certainly believe that we could have done better on the order booking by now, right?
I think that's the simple explanation we can give at this point.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided flat versus last year (about Rs 4,000 crore), with upside of 15-20% if mobilisation goes well; the ~Rs 15,000 crore order inflow target is reiterated but Q1 intake was thin (Rs 127 crore Bhutan order) and ~Rs 8,000 crore of recently won projects is still in mobilisation, backed by an order book and a Rs 1,672 crore HCC-share L1 position without firm timing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to 10.7% from 14.9%, but management guides a 13-14% run rate by year end as Rs 8,000 crore of mobilising projects convert to revenue; full-year average guided to mid-teens.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided flat versus last year (about Rs 4,000 crore), with only 15-20% upside (Rs 400-500 crore) if mobilisation goes well, and Q1 order intake was thin at Rs 127 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the Rs 15,000 crore order target and 13-14% margin but Q1 intake was Rs 127 crore against that target and some bids slipped about two months.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Order inflow is far behind a Rs 15,000 crore target, with only Rs 127 crore booked in Q1 and bids of about Rs 10,000 crore still under evaluation with a two-month slip; margin recovery to 13-14% depends on mobilisation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects significant nuclear orders in FY28 once SHANTI Act rules are published, with private orders six to eight months after rules; HCC is at pre-order stage.

rows.label: Order inflow recovery to Rs 15,000 cr target
rows.why: About Rs 10,000 crore of bids under evaluation (HCC share about Rs 7,750 crore) plus a Rs 1,672 crore HCC-share L1 position, against Q1 intake of only Rs 127 crore and a target of about Rs 15,000 crore.

rows.label: Debt prepayment and pledge release
rows.why: Rs 100 crore prepayment in August 2026 with larger prepayments under way on about Rs 2,000 crore total debt; pledges to lenders are to be removed as debt is repaid.

rows.label: Arbitration receivables of about Rs 1,700 crore
rows.why: Realisation expected over three to four years; government Vivad-se-Vishwas settlements at 65-85% of award could be pursued case by case, implying haircuts.

tone.note: Management was confident on the pipeline (Rs 10,000 crore bids under evaluation), deleveraging and the 13-14% margin recovery, but defensive on the Q1 margin fall of 4 points and the thin Rs 127 crore order intake; analysts pressed on order target achievability, arbitration timing and debt size.
